reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (≈600→1260/month) even though response times stay within SLA and no tariff change occurred, so the surge reflects genuine upstream billing errors rather than response capacity or rate changes. The best-supported mechanism is a change in billing import/validation processing around August: 59% of disputed bills were computed from ACTUAL meter reads (not estimates), so the majority of errors cannot be explained by estimate substitution and instead point to the billing import/validation step itself producing or accepting incorrect bills.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-02), and billing-import validation rule BV-17 — deployed 2026-08-01, comparing raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit conversion (E-13) — erroneously rejects valid high-consumption reads from firmware-v4.2 meters, which report in 0.1 m3 units (E-14), as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, driving estimate substitution for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (E-12). This confirmed mechanism explains at least the ESTIMATED minority (41%, E-04) of the Aug-Sep dispute surge.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
